answer: Behavioral Ridge Fingerprinting. Each agent’s outbound task mix is projected onto a fixed ridge of workload categories; the resulting plume vector must stay stable across sessions. Duplicates that split work to mimic distinct agents produce correlated vectors, which the coordinator flags when pairwise similarity exceeds threshold. An attacker must then diversify each clone’s task history at real compute cost, and pay per-identity jade renewal every epoch, making mass duplication economically visible and expensive.
